summary.destinationsDown: {count, plural, one {One destination stopped answering.} other {# destinations stopped answering.}} Copies bound for them are failing - open Destinations to see which.

table.partial: {name}: the copy landed in some destinations but not all. Open it to see which.
table.empty: Nothing is being backed up yet. Add a resource to start.
table.removeKeeps: Its {count, plural, one {# copy stays} other {# copies stay}} where they are and can still be restored. Delete them separately if you want them gone.
table.removeNoCopies: It has no copies yet, so nothing is lost.
table.lastFailed: The last copy did not land.
table.noPlans: No plans yet - make one under Plans

polarisDatabase.label: Polaris database
polarisDatabase.summary: Everything Polaris itself knows: accounts, apps, settings, history.

managedDatabase.label: Database
managedDatabase.summary: A database Polaris runs for one of your services.

minecraftWorld.label: Game world
minecraftWorld.summary: A Minecraft world, archived with saving paused so it is not caught mid-write.

deployVolume.label: Service data
deployVolume.summary: A volume one of your services keeps its data in.

mailServer.label: Mail server
mailServer.summary: A mail server's mailboxes, queue and keys, exported with the engine stopped so the copy is whole.

nasPath.label: Files
nasPath.summary: A folder on a storage connection.

plans.intro: A plan can be shared: put ten databases on one nightly plan and change the schedule once.
plans.none: No plans yet. Without one, things are backed up only when you ask.
plans.keeps: Keeps {copies, plural, =0 {any number of copies} other {# copies}}{days, plural, =0 {} other {, for # days}}{capped, select, yes {, under {size}} other {}} in each destination.
plans.usedBy: {count, plural, =0 {Nothing uses it} one {1 thing uses it} other {# things use it}}
plans.deleteBody: {count, plural, one {One thing is} other {# things are}} on this plan. They stay protected and become on-demand - no copies are deleted.

problems.name: Give the plan a name
problems.copies: That many copies is not a number
problems.days: That many days is not a number
problems.limit: Set at least one limit, or the copies pile up until the disk is full

plans.dialogIntro: How often a copy is taken, how many are kept in each destination, and where they go.
plans.goToHint: Every destination gets its own copy, written in this order. The first is the one the rest are replicated from.

notes.local: On this machine's data dir. Survives a mistake, not a dead disk.
notes.sourceLocal: Beside the thing itself. Instant, and lost with the disk it protects.
notes.connection: On a storage connection - a NAS, a bucket, a linked drive.
notes.host: On another server you have connected, over SSH.

destinations.intro: A plan can write to several. That is what makes a backup survive the machine it was taken on.
destinations.deleteBody: It still holds {count, plural, one {# copy} other {# copies}}. Polaris will refuse until they are gone, so they never become bytes nothing points at.
destinations.deleteEmpty: It holds nothing, so nothing is lost.
destinations.title: Add a destination
destinations.noConnections: No storage connections yet. Add one in Drive first.
destinations.folderHint: Everything is written under this, so backups never share a folder with anything else.

keys.rotated: New copies are sealed under the new key. Keep its recovery key too.
keys.added: Added. Copies sealed with it now open here.
keys.notAKey: That does not look like a recovery key
keys.intro: Copies are encrypted before they leave, with this account's backup key. Keep each key's recovery key somewhere other than this Polaris: without it, the copies cannot be opened once this Polaris is gone.
keys.none: No key yet. One is made with the first backup.
keys.made: Made {when} - {count, plural, one {# copy} other {# copies}}
keys.addHint: From another Polaris, to open the copies it sealed.
keys.name: backup key
keys.rotateBody: New copies are sealed under a new key. Copies already taken keep opening with the key they were sealed under.
keys.recoveryBody: Opens every copy this key sealed. Keep it in a password manager, not on this machine.

protect.intro: Everything here that is not being backed up yet. Pick what matters and give it a plan, or leave it on demand and back it up by hand.
protect.noDestination: There is nowhere to put a backup yet. Add a destination first.
protect.allProtected: Everything Polaris can find is already protected.
protect.planHint: A plan decides how often a copy is taken, how many are kept, and where they go. Without one, copies are only taken when you ask.

detail.gone: That protected item does not exist any more.
detail.partial: The last copy landed in some destinations but not all. What did land is still restorable.
detail.none: No copies yet. Back it up now, or give it a plan.
detail.encryptedHint: Encrypted with this account's backup key
detail.plainHint: Not encrypted: kept on the disk it copies, or taken before backups were encrypted
detail.noRestorePolaris: Polaris is running on this database, so it cannot be rewritten from here. Download the copy and load it with Polaris stopped.
detail.noRestore: This kind cannot be put back automatically - download the copy and restore it yourself.
detail.restoreBody: The copy in {where} will be written over what is there now.
detail.restoreWorld: It lands as a new level beside the one being played, so nothing is lost until you switch to it.
detail.restoreDatabase: A copy of the database as it is now is taken first and kept in this history; if that copy fails, nothing is restored.
detail.deleteOne: Every copy of it goes - the one in {where}. This cannot be undone.
detail.deleteAll: Every copy of it goes - all {count} of them. This cannot be undone.

page.title: Backups
page.description: What is protected, how often it is copied, and where those copies live.

errors.confirmRestore: Confirm the restore before it can run
errors.invalidPlan: Those plan details are not valid
errors.invalidDestination: Those destination details are not valid
errors.notAKey: That is not a backup key
errors.keyTooLong: A recovery key is shorter than that

refusals.besideSource: Copies beside the source are written by the source itself, not through a destination
refusals.otherMasterKey: This backup key was stored under a different master key. Add its recovery key to open the copies it sealed.
refusals.missingKey: This copy was sealed under a key this Polaris does not have. Add its recovery key first.
refusals.keyNotYours: That key belongs to somebody else here
refusals.keyMismatch: That recovery key does not match the key already stored here under the same id. Check it for a typo.
refusals.keyShape: A recovery key starts with {prefix}: and has three parts
refusals.keyId: The key's id is not one Polaris writes
refusals.keyBytes: The key itself is not 32 bytes
refusals.resourceGone: That protected item no longer exists
refusals.copyUnfinished: That copy did not finish being written
refusals.copyUnreadable: That copy cannot be read back
refusals.someDestinationMissing: One of those destinations does not exist
refusals.connectionMissing: That storage connection does not exist
refusals.destinationHoldsCopies: That destination still holds copies. Delete them first, or keep it so they stay reachable.
refusals.defaultDestination: That is the default destination. Make another one the default first.
refusals.nowhereForServer: There is nowhere to keep this server's copies
refusals.passphraseSealed: That copy was sealed with a passphrase, not a backup key
refusals.newerPolaris: That file was sealed by a newer Polaris
refusals.unknownKeyKind: That file names a key kind Polaris does not know
refusals.chunkSize: That file's chunk size is not one Polaris writes
refusals.passphraseSettings: That file's passphrase settings are out of range
refusals.truncatedChunk: That file ends in the middle of a chunk
refusals.wrongKey: That file does not open with this key, or has been changed
refusals.tooLarge: That file is too large to seal
refusals.truncatedHeader: That file ends before its header does
refusals.noDestination: There is nowhere to put this backup. Add a destination first.
refusals.databaseId: This database's id is missing from its record
refusals.databaseNoContainer: That database has no container to run the dump in
refusals.clusterInPlace: A Redis cluster cannot be restored in place: each master holds its own share of the keys. Nothing was changed.
refusals.clusterIntoSingle: This backup is of a Redis cluster: it holds each master's snapshot separately, and cannot be loaded into a single instance. Nothing was changed.
refusals.databaseHostMissing: The server this database runs on is not registered
refusals.clusterEmpty: That cluster has no nodes to take a backup of
refusals.volumeId: This volume's id is missing from its record
refusals.volumeUnreachable: That volume cannot be reached right now
refusals.folderConnection: This folder's connection is missing from its record
refusals.connectionUnreachable: That storage connection cannot be reached
refusals.mailServerId: This mail server's id is missing from its record
refusals.mailServerGone: That mail server no longer exists
refusals.mailServerSettingUp: That mail server has not finished setting up
refusals.mailServerStopped: That mail server's engine is not running
refusals.mailServerVolumes: The engine's volumes could not be found on its machine
refusals.notThisMailServer: That copy is not an export of this mail server
refusals.mailSafetyFailed: A copy of the server as it is now could not be taken, so nothing was restored
refusals.safetyFailed: Nothing was restored: a copy of what is there now could not be taken first.
refusals.safetyFailedWhy: Nothing was restored: a copy of what is there now could not be taken first ({why}).
refusals.cannotRestore: A {kind} cannot be put back from here - download it instead
refusals.noLongerKnows: Polaris no longer knows how to back up a {kind}
refusals.cannotDump: Polaris cannot dump a {engine} database yet
refusals.clusterPartial: {answered} of the cluster's {masters} masters answered, so no backup was taken: a copy of part of a cluster is not a backup of it.
